documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

53M transferring from another primary care office closer to his old address. Wants one place to call. Main issues are his neck, his back and his knees, and BP which he says has been fine on lisinopril.

HTN: lisinopril 10 daily for years per his account, takes it in the morning, no home cuff. No headaches beyond the usual, no chest symptoms.
Neck: told years ago he has arthritis and disc wear in the neck at two levels (C5-6, C6-7). Stiff after a long shift, no arm symptoms now.
Low back: L4-5 laminectomy this past spring at an outside spine group for leg pain, that's gone. Still gets a mechanical ache across the low back with bending and lifting. Back at work full duty since early summer.
Knees: both ache on stairs and after a day on the dock floor. No locking.
Uses ibuprofen 600 up to three times a day on bad days, cyclobenzaprine 5 at night now and then for spasm, Tylenol 500 for a headache.

PSH: L rotator cuff repair 2016; L4-L5 laminectomy 2022.
Allergies: sulfa (hives); shellfish, doesn't know what happened, was told as a kid to avoid it.
FH: father had neck arthritis that went on to myelopathy, and HTN. Mother with OA and osteoporosis. Older brother had a neck fusion for a pinched nerve.
SH: loads trucks at a distribution warehouse, 30+ years of lifting. Quit cigarettes 2019 after about 20 pack-years. A beer or two on weekends.

Exam: well-appearing, large frame. BP as charted. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Neck: reduced rotation both ways, no tenderness, Spurling negative bilaterally. Upper extremity strength, sensation and reflexes symmetric. Low back: healed midline scar, paraspinal tightness, straight leg raise negative. Knees: crepitus both, no effusion, stable.

A/P
1. HTN, at goal on lisinopril 10. Continue.
2. Cervical spondylosis with DDD, quiet. Lifting technique, keep moving.
3. Mechanical LBP after laminectomy, OA knees. As-needed meds as he has them.
4. Former smoker, qualifies for annual lung screening CT. Discussed what it is and what a false alarm looks like; he wants it. Ordered.
5. Tdap today. Baseline labs, HCV and HIV screening today.
6. Records release signed for prior PCP.
RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING, BASELINE
Indication: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2019.

Comparison: none.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear without consolidation or emphysema. Airways patent. No pleural effusion. Heart normal in size, no pericardial effusion. No enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. Mild degenerative change in the thoracic spine.

S: About 2 weeks of left-sided neck pain, now running into the left arm, with numbness of the thumb and index finger that comes and goes. No injury he can name, but 30-odd years of lifting. Ibuprofen takes the edge off; cyclobenzaprine helps him sleep. No gait trouble, no bowel or bladder change, right arm fine. Pain 6/10.

O: BP as charted. Neck: limited extension, left paraspinal tenderness. Left wrist extension slightly weak, 4+/5; grip and the rest of the arm full strength. Light touch reduced over the left thumb and index finger. Reflexes symmetric to my exam. Right arm normal. Gait normal.

A/P: Left cervical radicular symptoms on known C5-C7 spondylosis, with a mild motor finding. MRI C-spine ordered and PM&R referral placed. Continue ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed, no overhead lifting for now. Return or ED for spreading weakness, gait change, bladder or bowel symptoms.

reports.text:
MRI CERVICAL SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: left neck and arm pain with thumb and index numbness.
Technique: multiplanar multisequence imaging without contrast.
Comparison: none.
Findings: Alignment maintained. Vertebral body heights preserved; no fracture or marrow lesion. Cord normal in caliber and signal. Craniocervical junction normal.
C2-C3 through C4-C5: no significant disc bulge or stenosis.
C5-C6: disc desiccation and disc height loss with a broad degenerative bulge; canal and foramina adequate, no root compression.
C6-C7: disc desiccation and height loss. Left-sided disc herniation compresses the exiting left nerve root. No cord compression. Right foramen patent.
C7-T1: unremarkable.
Paraspinal soft tissues normal.
reports.conclusion:
1. Multilevel degenerative disc disease at C5-C6 and C6-C7.
2. Left-sided C6-C7 disc herniation with compression of the left exiting nerve root.
3. No cord compression.

documents.title: MRI result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Douglas, the MRI shows a disc bulging out at C6-C7 on the left and pressing on the nerve root there, on top of the wear-and-tear changes you already knew about. The spinal cord itself is fine. That fits your arm symptoms. You're on the books with PM&R next Wednesday and they'll go over treatment. Keep avoiding overhead lifting until then.

documents.title: RE: MRI result
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Consultation
documents.author: physiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL MEDICINE & REHABILITATION CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/03/2024
Reason for referral: neck pain with left arm symptoms.

History: 55-year-old warehouse loader with four weeks of neck pain that has steadily worsened and now travels into the left arm, with numbness in the thumb and index finger. He recalls no injury. Long history of heavy manual work. Known cervical spondylosis with disc degeneration at C5-C6 and C6-C7. Hypertension. Mechanical low back pain after L4-L5 laminectomy in 2022. Osteoarthritis of both knees. Left rotator cuff repair 2016.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily; ibuprofen 600 mg TID PRN; cyclobenzaprine 5 mg QHS PRN; acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria); shellfish (reaction unknown).
Family history: father with cervical spondylosis and myelopathy, hypertension; mother with osteoarthritis and osteoporosis; older brother with cervical radiculopathy treated with ACDF.
Social: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 5 years ago; 1-2 beers on weekends.

Examination: Alert, comfortable seated. Weakness of the left biceps and left wrist extensors. Sensation reduced over the lateral left forearm and the thumb and index finger. Left brachioradialis reflex diminished; other upper limb reflexes symmetric. Right arm normal. No Hoffmann sign, gait steady.

Imaging: MRI of the cervical spine 6/26/2024 reviewed: C6-C7 disc herniation with nerve root compression, on multilevel degenerative disc disease.

Impression: Left cervical radiculopathy, on a background of multilevel cervical spondylosis.

Plan:
- Physical therapy for cervical traction, mobility and scapular strengthening; referral sent.
- Continue ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed.
- Avoid heavy overhead lifting for the time being.
- Follow up here in 6 to 8 weeks.

Thank you for the referral.
Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival: 12/28/2025 10:40

CC: right arm weakness and numbness x 2 weeks.

HPI: 57M, warehouse loader, symptoms in the right arm since lifting a run of heavy boxes overhead at work about two weeks ago. Hard to grip; weakness worse squeezing hard or shoving doors open. Tingling runs from the shoulder along the back of the arm and forearm into the middle finger. Turning his head to the right or looking up for a while brings it on. Had a similar problem on the left side in July 2024, seen by PM&R and treated with therapy. Came today because he could not hold a coffee mug steady this morning. No bowel or bladder change, no leg symptoms, no fever.

PMH: cervical spondylosis with multilevel DDD C5-C6, C6-C7; cervical radiculopathy; hypertension; mechanical low back pain; bilateral knee OA.
PSH: L4-L5 lumbar laminectomy 2022; left rotator cuff repair 2016.
Meds: ibuprofen 600 mg TID PRN; cyclobenzaprine 5 mg QHS PRN; lisinopril 10 mg daily; acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria), shellfish.
FH: father cervical spondylosis with myelopathy, HTN; mother OA, osteoporosis; brother cervical radiculopathy s/p ACDF.
SH: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2019. Weekend beers.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. Neck: Spurling's maneuver reproduces the right arm symptoms. Triceps reflex decreased on the right compared with the left; biceps and brachioradialis symmetric. Strength reduced in right wrist extension and elbow extension; shoulder abduction and finger abduction full. Pinprick diminished over the right posterior forearm and the back of the third finger. Left arm normal. Legs: strength, sensation and reflexes normal, no clonus, gait normal.

Imaging: C-spine x-ray with degenerative narrowing and osteophytes, nothing acute.

MDM: radicular deficit in a right C7 distribution without myelopathic signs or red flags. Outpatient MRI appropriate.

Diagnosis: compression of the right C7 nerve root; cervical radiculopathy.

Disposition: discharged home 14:10. Continue home ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed. Avoid overhead lifting. Follow up with primary care within one week for outpatient MRI and specialist referral. Return for worsening weakness, leg symptoms, or bladder or bowel problems.

Date of visit: 01/21/2026
Referred for: right arm weakness and paresthesias.

Known to this clinic from 2024 for left cervical radiculopathy that resolved with therapy. Since mid-December, after overhead lifting at work, weakness and tingling in the right arm along the back of the arm into the middle finger. ED 12/28. Slowly improving, on modified duty.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily; ibuprofen 600 mg TID PRN; cyclobenzaprine 5 mg QHS PRN; acetaminophen 500 mg PRN. Allergies: sulfa, shellfish.

Exam: Right triceps reflex reduced. Right elbow extension and wrist extension 4/5, otherwise full strength. Pinprick decreased over the dorsal right forearm and third digit. Spurling positive right. No Hoffmann sign, gait normal. Left arm normal.

Impression: right C7 radiculopathy from C6-C7 foraminal disc herniation, on multilevel cervical spondylosis.

Four weeks into PT. Tingling down the right arm now only with long overhead looks, grip noticeably better, no dropped objects in two weeks. On light duty at work. Ibuprofen most days, cyclobenzaprine a few nights a week. Pain 2/10. Home BPs 120s-130s.

Exam: BP as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear. Right triceps 4+/5, wrist extension 4+/5. Triceps reflex still a bit reduced on the right. Pinprick nearly symmetric. Spurling mildly positive right. Gait normal.

A/P
1. Right C7 radiculopathy, improving with PT. PM&R follow-up in April; they'll decide on light duty from here. Return sooner if strength slips.
2. HTN controlled, lisinopril 10. BMP today.
3. Due for physical in September.

Exam: right triceps and wrist extensor strength 5/5, symmetric with the left. Sensation intact. Reflexes symmetric. Spurling negative.

Impression: right C7 radiculopathy, resolved with conservative care. No epidural injection or surgical referral needed.
Plan: home exercise program, full duty from 4/13/2026 with attention to overhead lifting technique. Return as needed.
